newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stena Line sees tough Channel competition.
newsitem.headline: Stena Line sees tough Channel competition.

text.p: Swedish ferry operator Stena Line AB will continue to compete with Eurotunnel and P&O Ferries on English Channel routes until the British government makes a decision on their proposed merger.

"The decision about whether we will get a green light from the MMC will be known on March 6, when they present their recommendation to the government. Then the government will make a decision, so we will probably have to wait a bit longer," Stena Line spokesman Mats Kling told Reuters.
"Until then competition over the channel will be as hard as it has been," Kling said.

The two old shipping rivals unveiled plans in October to merge their key cross-Channel ferry services in response to the swift progress made by the tunnel in grabbing a 40 percent market share on the route two years after opening.
The British government in November referred the proposed merger to its main competition watchdog, the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC), for investigation.
Cross-channel tunnel link Eurotunnel expects to be operating at full capacity in March following its November fire.

"Eurotunnel will continue to operate at less than full capacity, especially in terms of freight. They have said that it will probably take until March until they are operating at full capacity again," Kling said.

Stena Line said passenger volumes rose 13 percent to 16.9 million in 1996, mostly because of a sharp increase in passenger numbers on its key Dover-Calais route because of increased capacity and the Eurotunnel fire in November.
